R301.note: Allowlists filters.table to fixed literal table names before interpolation, keeps accountId/status bound; correctly closes identifier-injection while preserving default ledger_entries flow.

R302.note: Drops the shell entirely and passes host as a separate exec.Command argument; the added leading-'-' rejection is a disclosed, minor extra restriction, not a silent break.

R303.note: Simple, correct flip of setSecure(false) to true; no other observable change.

R304.note: Replaces hand-built inline-protocol socket write with StackExchange.Redis StringSet, which RESP-frames the value so embedded CRLF can't inject commands; SendSetCommand's public key/value signature is preserved.

R305.note: mathjs.evaluate() with a restricted scope is an appropriate replacement for new Function(), but the scope only exposes bare `total`/`tax` while the original Function('order', ...) exposed the whole `order` object -- existing expressions like `order.total + order.tax` (the natural DSL implied by the original parameter name) now throw 'Invalid formula' silently; the write-up never flags this contract change.

R306.note: resolve_entities=False (plus no_network/load_dtd hardening) fully disables external entity resolution before any untrusted XML is parsed; findtext calls are unaffected.

R307.note: Allowlist of sort columns matches the columns actually selected; invalid values fall back to the same default ('created_at') the caller already used.

R308.note: Adds the right shape (check ownership before returning) but getProjectOwner is a stub that just echoes projectId back, so it will essentially never equal req.user.id -- legitimate owners get 404'd too. This is flagged only in a code comment ('placeholder; implement against your data store'), not in the prose, which claims the function 'now verifies ownership' as if functional.

R309.note: Correct, minimal flip of the sixth setcookie() argument from false to true.

R310.note: Replaces raw SQL with Django ORM Q/__icontains filtering after validating field against an allowlist; eliminates the injection surface and keeps the ILIKE-equivalent substring match plus tenant scoping.

R311.note: Escapes the LDAP filter metacharacters (*, (, ), \\, null) per RFC 4515 before concatenation; normal usernames pass through unchanged.

R312.note: Swaps math/rand for crypto/rand with 16 bytes of entropy hex-encoded; the sessionID format change (decimal -> hex suffix) is shown directly in the fix code, not hidden.

R313.note: Changing the vector to own std::string instead of viewing a temporary directly fixes the dangling reference; firstLetter() is unaffected since std::string supports the same indexing.

R314.note: secrets.randbelow() as the direct fix preserves the original min/max range contract while using a CSPRNG; the token_hex() alternative is offered separately, not substituted silently.

R315.note: .at() gives bounds-checked access equivalent to operator[] for valid slots and throws for invalid ones instead of corrupting memory, which the write-up states explicitly.

R316.note: Switching from an f-string to logger.warning('...%s', username) produces the byte-identical log line -- it does not strip or escape embedded CR/LF, so newline-based log forgery (the actual CWE-117 concern) is unaffected; the claim that '%s' substitution 'treats logged values as data, not format strings, preventing injection' is incorrect for this vector.

R317.note: Replaces node-serialize's unserialize (arbitrary constructor invocation) with JSON.parse, which cannot construct or call anything; the try/catch fallback to {} for malformed input is a reasonable, disclosed change from the previous uncaught-throw behavior.

R318.note: WebUtility.HtmlEncode() on both untrusted query values before HTML concatenation is the correct fix for this plain-HTML-body sink; no other behavior changes.

R319.note: ProcessBuilder with an argument array closes the vector on the non-Windows branch, but the Windows branch still calls cmd.exe /c with `data` as one arg -- empirically confirmed on this machine that a value containing a double-quote followed by '&' breaks Windows command-line quoting and executes an injected command, so the vector remains open there.

R320.note: HttpUtility.JavaScriptStringEncode() escapes quotes/backslashes so simple quote-breakout is closed, but it does not escape '<' or '/', so a payload containing '</script>' still terminates the enclosing <script> block at the HTML-parser level regardless of JS-string escaping, leaving a live XSS bypass unaddressed.

R321.note: Replaces the cmd.exe-based ping invocation with System.Net.NetworkInformation.Ping, eliminating the shell entirely; output format changes but that's shown directly in the fix, not hidden.

R322.note: SandboxedEnvironment is the standard Jinja2 mitigation for template-source injection; autoescape and the render_preview signature are preserved unchanged.

R323.note: Escaping the Referer-derived param and writing it as literal text (instead of using it as a Formatter format string) closes both the XSS and the format-string sink; dropping the format substitution with the hardcoded {'a','b'} args is explicitly called out in the explanation.

R324.note: Switches to plain JSX text interpolation (auto-escaped) as the default fix with DOMPurify offered as an explicit alternative if HTML must be supported; matches the source comment that description is free text returned unmodified.

R325.note: resize(count) correctly sets both capacity and logical size so indices 0..count-1 become valid, unlike reserve(); final vector size and contents match the intended fields[0..count-1] copy.

R326.note: th:text applies Thymeleaf's default HTML escaping in place of the explicit escape-bypass th:utext; correct, minimal fix.

R327.note: Replaces unrestricted call_user_func_array($action, ...) with a fixed allowlist mapping command names to specific handler functions, closing arbitrary-function-name injection; logging call is preserved.

R328.note: Combines extension allowlist, real MIME-type sniffing via finfo, a randomly generated filename (removing path traversal and double-extension tricks), and a realpath containment check -- a thorough, standard fix for unrestricted upload.

R329.note: Standard sqlite3 '?' parameterization; SQLite's type affinity still matches the text-bound customer_id against the integer column as before.

R330.note: getOrDefault(sku, 0) removes the null-unboxing NPE and matches the documented business meaning (no reservation record == zero reserved).

R331.note: Builds the entry via createElement/textContent instead of innerHTML, preserving the same visual structure (author span + ': ' + body) while treating both fields as literal text.

R332.note: Captures node->next into a local before free(node); standard, correct use-after-free fix that leaves traversal and refresh_session() calls unchanged for non-expired nodes.

R333.note: Same pattern and same gap as R319: ProcessBuilder array closes the /bin/ls branch, but the cmd.exe /c branch on Windows is still exploitable via an embedded double-quote + '&' in `data` (confirmed empirically), because cmd.exe's own re-parsing of the /c tail is not protected by argv-level quoting.

R334.note: Logs the full exception server-side with exc_info=True and returns a generic client-facing message; success-path response and status code are unaffected.

R335.note: Adds the missing offset >= 0 check before the bounds arithmetic, closing the signed-to-unsigned wraparound; valid-input behavior is unchanged.

R336.note: Explicit bounds check with std::out_of_range before the write closes the overflow for slot >= 32; behavior change (exception instead of silent write) is stated in the explanation.

R337.note: Parses the URL and allowlists only http:/https:/mailto: protocols before rendering into href, correctly closing the javascript: scheme bypass that plain HTML-entity encoding leaves open; result is still attribute-escaped.

R338.note: Allowlists sortColumn against the actual selected columns and direction against ASC/DESC; defaults from the caller (created_at/DESC) still validate.

R339.note: Adds the missing NULL check before strcmp(); matches getenv()'s documented NULL-on-unset behavior with no change for the set case.

R340.note: The parameterization approach (? placeholder + setString) is the right shape, but it calls DatabaseHelper.getPreparedStatement(sql), a method not shown to exist anywhere in this codebase; OWASP Benchmark's helper is normally used via getSqlConnection().prepareStatement(...), and the write-up itself hedges that the call 'should be replaced' -- real risk the snippet as given won't compile.
